note: The claims t_v90params.cpp makes about V90Parameters, each broken on purpose.  The set is deliberately weighted towards the four things `setToDefault` READS -- a table of 339 constants is easy to check and the arithmetic around it is not, and the divisor mutation below is the defect this file's first run actually had. A destructor-store mutation in this file WAS recorded `equivalent` on the grounds that GCC deletes a store to `*this` in a destructor. That was measured and true; `-fno-lifetime-dse` in CXXFLAGS then restored GCC 3.4.2's semantics and the store survives, so the mutation is caught and the verdict is retired. If that flag is ever dropped, this entry goes back to being uncatchable -- and the symptom will be a NOT CAUGHT, not a compile error.

label: the power reduction divides by 10, not 5
the power reduction scale is 1.0, not 0.5
the printed fraction is scaled by 10, not 100
the printed whole part keeps its sign
why: `tempPR` is `unsigned int` and the object divides it by 5, so `tempPR / 5` is at most 0x33333333 and `(int)(tempPR / 5)` can never be negative; `pr` is that times 0.5f and is therefore never negative either.  So `whole < 0` is unreachable over the WHOLE input domain and not merely over the fixture's.  The object has the same dead code -- `fabs` at .text+0x2a731 and `cltd; xor %edx,%eax; sub %edx,%eax` at +0x2a78f -- and it is reproduced because it is in the object, not because anything can reach it.  The identical argument covers the `frac < 0` line below.
